key_concepts: Plants have common basic parts: roots, stems, and leaves.
Roots grow underground and hold the plant in place.
Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
Stems support and hold the leaves.
Stems transport water from roots to leaves.
Leaves receive water and use sunlight to make food.
Plant parts vary in shape, size, and form among different plants.
Stems can be herbaceous or woody.
Some roots and stems store food, such as carrot roots and ginger stems.
Cactus leaves are sharp spikes that protect the plant from animals.
Plants need water and nutrients from the soil to stay healthy.
Fertilizers add nutrients to soil, helping plants grow healthier and more fruitful.
